newsitem.title: UK: Finland can join EMU without Sweden-Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: Finland can join EMU without Sweden-Central Bank.

text.p: Finland can definitely join European monetary union (EMU) in 1999 even if Sweden does not, Bank of Finland Governor Sirkka Hamalainen said in an interview with Central Banking magazine.
"I believe definitely so," Hamalainen said when asked if Finland could join EMU's first wave without Sweden - a key competitor.
"The room for depreciation of countries outside EMU will depend on the rules linking them to the euro, either formally in ERM2 or informally, even if floating," she said.
And even if Sweden is left outside the first phase of EMU, which is not certain, Hamalainen said she was confident authorities there would peruse "responsible monetary and exchange rate policies."
Hamalainen, however, said Europe as a whole would have many problems if EMU's third stage does not start in 1999.
"Then, we would have many problems all over Europe and not just in Finland. However, I would stress that we must build a stable European monetary system."
"If the interpretation of the criteria in the Maastricht treaty or in the proposed stability pact are too flexible, the European Central Bank would face big difficulties," she added.
